arxiv-2401-09373.title: On the Archimedean Positivstellensatz in Real Algebraic Geometry
arxiv-2401-09373.creator: Konrad Schmüdgen
arxiv-2401-09373.description: Abstract . A variant of the Archimedean Positivstellensatz is proved which is based on Archimedean semirings or quadratic modules of generating subalgebras. It allows one to obtain representations of strictly positive polynomials on compact semi-algebraic sets by means of smaller sets of squares or polynomials. A large number of examples is developed in detail. AMS Subject Classification (2020) .

arxiv-2405-00590.title: Nonlinear Poisson effect in affine semiflexible polymer networks
arxiv-2405-00590.creator: Jordan L. Shivers, Fred C. MacKintosh
arxiv-2405-00590.description: Abstract Stretching an elastic material along one axis typically induces contraction along the transverse axes, a phenomenon known as the Poisson effect. From these strains, one can compute the specific volume, which generally either increases or, in the incompressible limit, remains constant as the material is stretched.

arxiv-2405-04635.title: Mysterious anomalies in Earth’s atmosphere and strongly interacting Dark Matter
arxiv-2405-04635.creator: Ariel Zhitnitsky, Marios Maroudas
arxiv-2405-04635.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ariel Zhitnitsky, Marios Maroudas. It has been recently argued in [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] that numerous enigmatic observations remain challenging to explain within the framework of conventional physics. These anomalies include unexpected correlations between temperature variations in the stratosphere, the total electron content of the Earth’s atmosphere, and earthquake activity on one hand, and the positions of planets on the other. Decades of collected data provide statistically significant evidence for these observed correlations.

arxiv-2510-11537.title: An Encoder-Integrated PhoBERT with Graph Attention for Vietnamese Token-Level Classification
arxiv-2510-11537.creator: Ba-Quang Nguyen
arxiv-2510-11537.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ba-Quang Nguyen. In this paper, we propose a novel neural architecture named TextGraphFuseGAT , which integrates a pretrained transformer encoder (PhoBERT) with Graph Attention Networks (GAT) for token-level classification tasks. The proposed model constructs a fully connected graph over the token embeddings produced by PhoBERT, enabling the application of a GAT layer to capture rich inter-token dependencies beyond those modeled by sequential context alone. To further enhance contextualization, a Transformer-style self-attention layer is applied on top of the graph-enhanced embeddings.

pmc-10621189.title: Faculty development for translational simulation: a qualitative study of current practice
pmc-10621189.creator: Victoria Brazil, Eve Purdy, Alexander El Kheir, Rebecca A. Szabo
pmc-10621189.description: BackgroundTranslational simulation is focused directly on healthcare quality, safety, and systems. Effective translational simulation design and delivery may require knowledge and skills in areas like quality improvement and safety science. How translational simulation programs support their faculty to learn these skills is unknown.

pmc-11677334.title: Impact of Intraoperative Opioid Use and a Combined Anesthesia Regimen in Patients Undergoing Radical Prostatectomy for Prostate Cancer in a Single-Center Cohort
pmc-11677334.creator: Julian Marcon, Robert Bischoff, Kaspar Rattenhuber, Michael Chaloupka, Darjusch Askari, Jan-Friedrich Jokisch, Armin J Becker, Paulo L Pfitzinger, Patrick Keller, Elena Berg, Christian G Stief, Daniel Siegl, Christian Kowalski, Alexander Buchner, Nikolaos Pyrgidis, Philipp Weinhold, Markus W Hollman
pmc-11677334.description: Introduction: Higher intraoperative opioid doses may be associated with worse long-term oncological outcomes after radical prostatectomy (RP) for prostate cancer. We aimed to evaluate the impact of higher doses of intraoperative opioids and type of anesthesia on biochemical recurrence (BCR) and mortality after RP in a high-volume tertiary center.

pmc-12436884.title: Neurological Soft Signs in Patients with Schizophrenia May be Related to Treatment Resistance
pmc-12436884.creator: S Elmas, A Üçok
pmc-12436884.description: IntroductionMotor abnormalities in schizophrenia are important as they are measurable objective parameters. Neurological soft signs (NSS), which are one of the primary motor abnormalities, are minor motor and sensory abnormalities that cannot be localised to a specific brain region, reflect the areas of sensory integration, motor coordination and motor sequencing.

pmc-12470464.title: Evidence on Non-Invasive Respiratory Support During Flexible Bronchoscopy: A Narrative Review
pmc-12470464.creator: María Hidalgo Sánchez, Manel Luján, Sergio Alcolea Batres, Julia Álvarez del Vayo, Pablo Mariscal-Aguilar, Carlos Carpio, Rodolfo Álvarez-Sala Walther, Adriano Peris
pmc-12470464.description: Background: Flexible bronchoscopy (FB) is a widely used diagnostic and therapeutic procedure in patients with pulmonary disease, many of whom are at risk of gas exchange impairment. FB may exacerbate hypoxaemia due to increased airway resistance, alveolar derecruitment, and haemodynamic fluctuations. Objectives: To assess the effectiveness of non-invasive respiratory support strategies in preventing oxygen desaturation and respiratory complications during FB.

pmc-12561357.title: Aggressive Behavior in Adolescents and Emerging Adults: The Psychometrics of the Portuguese Brief Peer Conflict Scale (Brief-PCS)
pmc-12561357.creator: Paula Vagos, Pedro F S Rodrigues, Josefa N S Pandeirada, Monica A Marsee, Gengfeng Niu
pmc-12561357.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The Brief Peer Conflict Scale (Brief-PCS) has been shown to be psychometrically suitable for assessing the combination of the forms and functions of aggressive behavior in adolescence. However, its validity, invariance, and utility across other age groups remains unexplored. The current study aims to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Brief-PCS in community samples of adolescents and emerging adults, and to compare self-reported aggression across these age groups and by sex.

pmc-12672305.title: Allergy-unrelated eosinophil activation in the peripheral blood of children with neurodevelopmental disorders
pmc-12672305.creator: Wenjing Ji, Muhan Li, Chenlu Yang, Yuanyuan Lu, Aimin Liang
pmc-12672305.description: BackgroundNeurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are increasingly associated with immune dysregulation, but eosinophil activation independent of allergic diseases remains unexplored in this population.MethodsPeripheral-blood eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) mRNA expression was quantified in 55 children with NDDs—including developmental delay (DD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), communication disorder, and tic disorder—and 32 typically developing controls.

pmc-12968938.title: Disparities in Access to Cystic Fibrosis Therapy Across Countries
pmc-12968938.creator: Bulent Karadag
pmc-12968938.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cystic fibrosis has been transformed by the development of CFTR modulator therapies, with substantial improvements in survival and quality of life. However, access to these therapies remains profoundly unequal worldwide. The greatest benefits have been realized in high‐income countries, while people with cystic fibrosis in low‐ and middle‐income countries and underserved populations within high‐income settings continue to face limited access and poorer outcomes.

pmc-13087092.title: Depression Mediates the Association Between Ambient Air Pollution and Gastrointestinal/Liver Diseases: A Prospective Cohort Study
pmc-13087092.creator: Yanqi Kou, Shicai Ye, Mouji Liang, Lei Ge, Ling Qin, Yanping Ha, Yuan Tian, Botao Luo, Chunyi Wu, Liping Zhan, Ke Yang, Zhuoyan Lu, Yuping Yang
pmc-13087092.description: BackgroundThe escalating burden of gastrointestinal (GI) and liver diseases poses a critical public health challenge, with emerging evidence implicating air pollution as a modifiable risk factor. However, the mechanistic pathways, particularly the mediating role of depression in the pollution‐disease nexus, remain underexplored.

pmc-13200411.title: Factors associated with interruption in treatment among pregnant and breastfeeding women living with HIV on ART in South Sudan
pmc-13200411.creator: Silvestro Ojja, Amy Benson, Megan Swanson, Elizabeth Carter, Katherine A Battey, Sarah Auma, Akech Awan, Alex Bolo, Michele Montandon, Sudhir Bunga
pmc-13200411.description: BackgroundContinuity of HIV treatment among pregnant and breastfeeding women (PBFW) living with HIV is challenging in South Sudan. Understanding factors associated with interruption in treatment (IIT) among PBFW on antiretroviral therapy (ART) may inform programmatic interventions to improve care and continuity of treatment.MethodsA retrospective cohort analysis of records of PBFW on ART in twenty health facilities was conducted.

pmc-13232807.title: Individual and school-level factors associated with suspected pediatric eye disorders and referral adherence in an enhanced school-based vision screening program in Ghana
pmc-13232807.creator: Afua O. Asare, Priscilla Ablordeppey, Enoch Ansah-Asiedu, Emmanuel T. Doku, Gabriel K. Agbeshie, Seyram A. Gle, Nana Akwasi Owusu Mensah, Ruby E. Adikah, Christiana Nyarko Yeboah, Debora A. Baidoo, Christine K. Darko, Elisha E. Arkhurst, Melissa H. Watt, Eldrick A. Acquah, Hornametor Afake, Sylvia A
pmc-13232807.description: Evidence on how social and school-level contexts shape pediatric vision screening outcomes is limited, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. We examined the association between individual and contextual factors and vision screening outcomes in a pilot enhanced school-based vision screening program (ESVSP) in Kumasi, Ghana.

pmc-13269511.title: Influence of cell culture parameters on oxygen diffusion and cell distribution in 3D-porous scaffolds for bone tissue engineering: finite element modeling and experimental verification
pmc-13269511.creator: Alireza Saatchi, Hadi Seddiqi, Ghassem Amoabediny, Marco N Helder, Behrouz Zandieh-Doulabi, Jenneke Klein-Nulend
pmc-13269511.description: Successful bone tissue engineering using 3D-porous scaffolds is hampered by insufficient oxygen diffusion and non-uniform cell distribution, which are determined by cell culture parameters. Here we aimed to investigate the influence of cell culture parameters on oxygen diffusion and cell distribution in 3D-porous scaffolds during 15-days by finite-element (FE) modeling. Osteosarcoma cells were cultured in 3D-porous silk scaffolds under 0.

pmc-13353166.title: Attitudes, interest and involvement of midwives in an RCT: A qualitative study with a phenomenological approach
pmc-13353166.creator: Maria Panzeri, Teresa Terenghi, Sara Ornaghi, Sara E. Borrelli, Antonella Nespoli, Anna Locatelli, Simona Fumagalli
pmc-13353166.description: INTRODUCTIONIn order to improve evidence-based, woman-centered care, research is an essential component of midwifery professional practice. The active involvement of clinical midwives in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remains modest, despite its acknowledged relevance. The study aims to explore attitudes, interest, and involvement of midwives in an RCT.
